body:
<!-- pr-reviewer: 713cfe0f10d5e52e6e192edaf479890544ac882e -->
**Needs changes before merge.** One regression: editing a built-in plate (`SetPlate`) now unmounts every fixture standing on it.

### What looks good
- Load notes: `plate_dto::link_from` and `modvise_dto::params_from` push one note per dropped key, and `apply.rs` now reports each name `drop_dangling` returns. Every `tracing::warn!` drop path in those readers now also writes a note, and the file still loads. The new test checks four dropped keys and asserts exactly one note for each.
- `UpdateModel` keeps the plate snapshot boxed (`Option<Box<(FixtureDef, Unmounts)>>`), so clippy's `large_enum_variant` stays quiet. `invert` puts the marker and the riders' markers back exactly. A model that isn't a plate gets `plate: None`, so its path is unchanged.
- `LocateFixture` now runs the same `MoveFixture::rider_warnings` check and joins the result with `fixture_clash::join`, which also removes duplicates.
- `square_edges`: I tested this one directly. A 45° plate is still refused as turned. 3°, 1° and 0.2° turns are refused by the lattice check. A 45° diamond with one axis-aligned flat (one-sided chamfer, flat depth 10 to 90 mm) is still refused. The ear and chamfer cases from the issue are now accepted.
- The split of `fixture.rs` into `fixture_move.rs` only moves code. `MoveFixture` is re-exported, `require_writable` became `pub(super)`, and `MoveFixture::new` gives the same warnings as before, now through `join`. The new module has its provenance line, the two files are 325 and 108 lines, and the PR has no `unwrap` or `expect` outside tests.
- The small fixes (stud message, `warn!` on save, removing the duplicated hint, the outdated doc line) are all in place. No PNGs, no process files, no dependency changes. `Changelog:` is present and the body ends with `Fixes #826`.

### Local results (trial-merged with current upstream `main`, clean merge)
| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test -p camcraft-app --no-run` | built |
| app `fixture_plate_followups` | 4 passed |
| app `fixture_keys_lenient` | 3 passed |
| app `fixture_plate` | 7 passed |
| app `fixture_plate_detect` | 3 passed |
| app `fixture_plate_riders` | 6 passed |
| app `fixture_locate` | 11 passed |
| app `fixtures` | 14 passed |
| app `mod_vise_plate` | 6 passed |
| app `builtin_accessory` | 3 passed |
| app `project_roundtrip` | 71 passed |
| app `commands_undo` | 32 passed |
| app `repair_model` / `scripting` / `import` / `builtin_vise` / `mcp_plate` / `fixture_locate_stock` / `carried_fixtures_cache` (other `UpdateModel` paths) | 4 / 18 / 22 / 9 / 1 / 3 / 6 passed |
| ui `--lib fixture` (CWD `crates/ui`) | 44 passed |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

All of these pass, but none of them checks a rider's mount after a `SetPlate`. That is the gap described below.

### Requested before merge
1. **`SetPlate` unmounts its riders (regression).** `SetPlate` (`crates/app/src/commands/fixture_plate.rs:200`, `:228-229`) builds an `UpdateModel` for the new slab mesh. With this PR, `UpdateModel::apply` (`crates/app/src/commands/update_model.rs:132-137`) sees a plate and does two things: it clears the plate's grid, and it calls `Unmounts::write(world, true)`, which sets `plate.mount = None` on every rider. `Swap::write` then puts the plate's new grid back, but it only writes the riders' poses, never their markers. After a plain plate edit, every fixture on the plate has lost its grid location.
   - **Effect:** the riders are re-seated in the right place but are no longer attached to the plate. A later `MoveFixture` or `LocateFixture` of the plate leaves them behind without any message (`carried()` is empty), and the plate's own placement checks no longer see them.
   - **Reproduced on the merged tree** with a throwaway test (not pushed): `InsertPlate` 300 x 300, block on B2, `SetPlate` with pitch_x 25.4. Afterwards the rider's mount is `None` and `MoveFixture::new(plate, ..).carried()` is `[]`. On `main`, `UpdateModel` doesn't touch `FixtureDef` and the mount is kept.
   - **Fix (one option):** let `SetPlate` build its update without the plate drop. For example, add a crate-private `UpdateModel::reshaping(..)` constructor (or a flag) that skips the `plate` snapshot, because `SetPlate` re-seats its own riders and writes its own grid. Please also pin it: add an assertion to `fixture_plate.rs`'s H10 edit (or to `fixture_plate_riders`) that the rider is still mounted after `SetPlate`, and that a following `MoveFixture` of the plate carries it.
   - **Please check the other wrappers too.** `ImportFixture` wraps `UpdateModel` and ends with the same markers either way, and undo there is fine. The built-in vise and accessory edits wrap it too, but those models are never plates, so they're unaffected.

### Questions / notes (not blocking)
- **`square_edges` shapes.** A 45° turned lattice on an outline with long axis-aligned flats at the greatest X and least Y (flat depth 30 to 90 mm on a 250 mm diamond) is now accepted as a staggered grid. Under the old least-edge rule, the mirrored least-X and least-Y version was already accepted, so this is the same heuristic applied to the other sides, not a new kind of acceptance. Those holes really are a checkerboard in X/Y, so hole positions stay exact. I don't see a mis-placement here; I'm only noting the limit of the rule. A pure turn at 0.01° is accepted through the regular-grid path (0.044 mm drift over 250 mm, inside `ON_NODE`). That behaviour already exists and this PR doesn't change it.
- `crates/app/src/project/plate_dto.rs:43`, `:51` and `:56`: the new `notes.push` lines are indented one level deeper than the `tracing::warn!` above them. Running `cargo fmt` on the file would fix it.
- `crates/app/src/project/apply.rs` is 826 lines and this PR adds 2. Not blocking; it's the existing oversized file.
- I didn't find any other path that changes a mesh outside `UpdateModel`. Every other `set_facets` call is a stock re-mesh, an insert or spawn, or a delete/untag/setup undo restore. Load (`project/apply.rs`) writes facets directly, as it should.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

<!-- pr-reviewer: 698003feee23ff3492e9b7072ef25fbe156e5f0b -->
**Ready for the maintainer to merge.** This is a delta review of `713cfe0f..698003fe` (one commit, `fix(app): SetPlate keeps its riders mounted`), and it fixes the blocker from the previous review.

### What looks good
- **`UpdateModel::keeping_plate()`** (`crates/app/src/commands/update_model.rs:100-107`) is `pub(crate)` and `#[must_use]`, and it only clears the plate snapshot. The only caller is `SetPlate` (`crates/app/src/commands/fixture_plate.rs:200`). I grepped every `UpdateModel::new` call, and each one that really replaces a mesh still builds the full snapshot, so a re-imported plate still loses its grid and its riders: the UI re-import (`crates/ui/src/state.rs:3736`), `cam.import` / the script and MCP import (`crates/app/src/script/api.rs:59`), `RepairModel` (`repair_model.rs:74`) and `ImportFixture` (`import_fixture.rs:63`). The built-in vise (`builtin_vise.rs:130`) and accessory (`accessory.rs:159`) edits never act on a plate, so they get `plate: None` either way.
- **The #833 `SetPlate` laws are unchanged.** `jaws_after_reseat` still runs before the update is built, so a jaw pushed into the stock is refused by name (`mod_vise_plate::a_plate_edit_that_pushes_a_jaw_into_the_stock_is_refused_by_name`). Every rider and the new slab are still clash-checked where they land (`fixture_plate_riders::an_edited_plates_riders_are_clash_checked_where_they_land`). Both tests pass.
- **The pin, `fixture_plate_riders::an_edited_plate_keeps_its_riders_mounted`**, checks everything the earlier review asked for. After `SetPlate` the rider is still mounted on the plate, a following `MoveFixture` of the plate carries it, and undo/redo restore both the pose and the mount exactly.
- **Spot-check:** I reverted only the `.keeping_plate()` call locally, on the merged tree. The pin then fails at `fixture_plate_riders.rs:235` ("still mounted after the edit") and the other 6 tests in the suite still pass. With the call restored, all 7 pass. So the test pins this exact fix.
- The `plate_dto.rs` change only re-indents lines. It changes no tokens and no logic.

### Local results (trial-merged with current upstream `main`, clean merge)
| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test -p camcraft-app --no-run` | built |
| app `fixture_plate_followups` | 4 passed |
| app `fixture_plate` | 7 passed |
| app `fixture_plate_riders` | 7 passed (6 + the new pin) |
| app `mod_vise_plate` | 6 passed |
| app `mcp_plate` | 1 passed |
| app `commands_undo` | 32 passed |
| app `repair_model` | 4 passed |
| app `import` | 22 passed |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

### Requested before merge
None.

### Questions / notes (not blocking)
- `crates/app/src/project/plate_dto.rs:37`: the re-indent fixed lines 43, 50 and 55, but it moved the first `notes.push` (inside the nested `Err(why)` arm) from 16 spaces to 12. That line is now one level shallower than the `tracing::warn!` above it. This is cosmetic only, so it can wait for a later touch of the file.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
